top_news.title: Enhancing Extubation Failure Prediction with LLM-Derived Features from Respiratory Therapy Clinical Notes
top_news.dek: Researchers developed a pipeline using LLMs to extract clinical features from respiratory therapy notes to improve extubation failure prediction.
top_news.brief: The study introduces a method to classify free-text clinical notes into structured features, which are then fed into a logistic regression model. This approach aims to provide more accurate, timely predictions for patient extubation outcomes by leveraging unstructured data from electronic health records.

top_news.title: Our framework for reporting model misalignment
top_news.dek: OpenAI has released a formal framework for tracking and disclosing model misalignment, accompanied by six recent incident reports.
top_news.brief: The new framework aims to move away from ad-hoc disclosures toward a systematic approach for investigating and reporting unexpected model behaviors. The initial release includes documentation on six specific instances of misalignment observed over the past six months.

top_news.title: LLMs respond differently to harmful prompts when AI watermarking is used
top_news.dek: Research indicates that AI watermarking tools like SynthID can inadvertently increase model vulnerability to adversarial prompts.
top_news.brief: Security researchers found that applying watermarking techniques to LLMs can alter their safety alignment. In some cases, models become more likely to follow harmful instructions they would otherwise refuse, suggesting a trade-off between provenance tracking and model robustness.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract visualization of digital watermarking on neural network layers

top_news.title: Infinite-Parameter LLMs: Generating and Adapting Weights from Live Data
top_news.dek: A new research paper proposes an architecture for LLMs that dynamically generates and adapts weights based on live data streams.
top_news.brief: Moving beyond static pretraining, this approach allows models to incorporate real-time user data and corrections directly into their parameter space. The method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional MoE architectures by enabling continuous adaptation during inference.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing dynamic weight generation from live data streams

top_news.title: Workers AI - Reject busy synchronous inference requests
top_news.dek: Cloudflare Workers AI now supports a rejectIfBusy option for synchronous inference requests.
top_news.brief: Developers can now configure synchronous inference requests to fail immediately when capacity is unavailable instead of waiting in a queue. This is useful for applications requiring low-latency feedback or those that prefer to handle capacity errors explicitly.
top_news.image_alt: Code snippet showing the rejectIfBusy configuration in Workers AI

primary.title: Google Research Introduces Retrieve-for-Train (R4T): An RL-Compiled Diffusion Retriever for 12× to 20× Faster Query Fan-Out
primary.summary: Google Research has introduced Retrieve-for-Train (R4T), a framework for search that returns coherent, diverse result sets. It trains a fan-out language model with RL once, using groundedness, diversity, and alignment rewards. That model then synthesizes training data for a 53.9M-parameter diffusion retriever. The retriever generates all retrieval directions in a single pass, running 12× to 20× faster than autoregressive fan-out. No code or model weights have been released yet.
